Action.description:
A write the assistant made, as the turn reports it (every direct write is reported
with its consequences).

consequences.description: What it newly caused in each journey it changed.

nodes.description:
The nodes it wrote, in key order (a direct change is reported with the nodes
it affected, which the panel links to); none for a write to no journey's nodes.

receipt.description: Which patch, where, and the revision it produced.

report.description:
What it did, in words: each kind of change once in the order its patch first
makes it, the nodes it wrote, and what it newly caused, each node as
`journey/node` code ("Added a note, marked done: `j_one/n_kickoff`."). The panel
shows it and the conversation keeps it, the same text.

oneOf.description:
A write whose patch id was applied before, with the same content: answered from that
write's receipt, and not applied again.
Drafted as a proposal for the user to review and apply.

destination.description: Its destination, under which it is addressed.

oneOf.description: An open proposal discarded, at the assistant's hand.

Actor.description: Who made a change: a user, or an agent acting for one.

agent.description: The agent acting for the user, if any.

AffectedNodes.description:
Some nodes an answer's effect names: how many in all, and the first
`explanation_entry_count_max` of them in tree order.

nodes.description: The first of them, in tree order, at most `explanation_entry_count_max`.

total.description: How many nodes there are in all.

AgentId.description: Starts with "ag_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

AgentSignIn.description: One way an agent signs in to the MCP server.

oneOf.description:
The built-in OAuth server: a browser step on first use; the agent is recorded beside
the person.

Behind IAP, the relay to Google: a browser step with Google, the client signing in on
the machine it runs on.

Tailscale, either mode: no sign-in step, from a machine in the tailnet signed in as a
person.
The dev provider without a token: every request it accepts is its dev user.

AgentToken.description: An agent token as its user's list shows it: never the secret.

agent.description: The agent the token acts as.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked, if it was.

Annotation.description:
A journey-authored note or link on a node or on the journey itself, attributed and
timestamped from the patch that added it.

edited_at.description: When it was last edited, if ever.

AnnotationBody.description: A note or link as its author writes it: the part an add or edit carries.

AnswerEffects.description:
What answering a decision does, per choice, and the static lines every answer
of a date or identity decision carries.

applies.description:
Whether the decision's answer is in effect: it is relevant, and not skipped. When not,
no answer changes any other node's relevance and every choice's effect is empty.

choices.description:
One entry per choice of a boolean, single-choice, or multi-choice decision, in the
decision's order (`false` before `true`); none for the other answer types.

fills_role.description: The role its answer fills, for an identity or identity-list decision.

pins.description: The milestone its answer pins, for a date decision.

AnswerText.description:
A text answer: any text up to the body limit, empty included (an empty submission is an
answer).

AnswerValue.description:
A decision's submitted answer. Submitted empty text or an
empty list is answered.

AppliedOver.description:
What a write that was applied past other people's changes tells its writer: the revisions
it named that others' writes had moved, and what those writes changed, none of which this
write changes. The writer's view is behind by exactly those changes, so it reads again
before its next write.

conflicts.description: The revisions the write named that had moved on.

intervening.description: What the commits since those revisions changed.

AppliedReceipt.description:
What the report of an applied write names: the patch, its domain, and the revision it
produced.

domain.description: The domain it was committed to.

revision.description: The revision it produced.

AssistantRequest.description:
`POST /api/journeys/{id}/assistant` and `POST /api/routes/{id}/draft/assistant`: one message of
the caller's conversation about that journey or draft.

AttachmentKey.description: Starts with "a_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

AuthKind.description: The kinds of sign-in a host can offer.

oneOf.description: A static token or named dev user.
OAuth or OIDC against a registered provider.
The built-in OAuth server for MCP clients.
Google Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy's signed assertion.
The browser host's single local login.

kind.description: What kind of provider it is.

Because.description: Why a write became a proposal.

oneOf.description: It changes structure, or writes a route or its draft.
The assistant drafted it as a proposal itself.

Blocker.description: A dependency that blocks a node (Gating: Blocked).

date.description:
The date the dependency is scheduled for, while it is held for a date ahead, so what
waits on it can say when.

Bound.description: A derived date bound and the chain that produced it.

chain.description: The chain from a pin, actual, or today that produced it.

Bypass.description:
A guard bypass as stored, written by a completion that went ahead anyway: why when a
reason was given, and the specific failures present, which say the guards bypassed.

failures.description: The failures present when the completion went ahead.

reason.description: Why, when a reason was given.

Caller.description: The caller and the identities their verified emails name.

agent.description: The agent acting for them, when the request carries an agent token.

logins.description: The logins they sign in with, by provider and subject.

Capabilities.description: The capabilities document (`GET /api/capabilities`): what this host offers.

assistant.description: Whether the in-app assistant is available.

auth.description: How people sign in, in the order the host asks.

mcp.description: How an agent reaches this host's MCP server; null where the host serves none.

sse.description: Whether the host streams revision ticks over SSE.

version.description:
The release this host runs (a version, or `dev` for a build without one); null where no
server binary serves the page.

Chain.description: A chain of constraints, with the dates fixed on it.

constraints.description: The constraints, in order along the chain.

fixed.description: The pins and actuals on it.

total.description:
How many constraints and fixed dates the whole chain holds, when a server response
cut it to `explanation_entry_count_max` of each; absent for a chain given whole. The
rest pages through the explanations of the value the chain explains.

ChainList.description:
The contradictory chains a rejection lists: at most
`chain_count_per_rejection_max`, and whether there were more.

chains.description: The chains found, up to the limit.

more.description: The search was cut short at the limit.

ChecklistCount.description: How much of a checklist is ticked.

id.description: The id a tick names; unique within the checklist.

ChildEntry.description: One child in a node's detail.

display_state.description: The state every surface shows for it.

Choice.description:
One choice of a single- or multi-choice decision: an id that answers and conditions use,
and an optional label. Written as the bare id when it has no label.

ChoiceEffect.description:
What one answer to a decision does to the journey's scope, from a three-valued
re-evaluation of relevance under that answer: never a full derive.

answer.description:
The whole answer evaluated: a boolean, a choice, or (for a multi choice) the current
answer with `choice` toggled.

choice.description: The choice id, for a single or multi choice.

current.description:
This is the recorded answer (for a multi choice: `choice` is in it, so the answer
evaluated removes it).

decided_later.description:
Nodes that would stay undecided because they hang on another decision still to be
answered, which this answer opens or leaves open.

drops.description:
Nodes the answer settles as not relevant. Nodes that would still hang on another
unanswered decision are `decided_later`, never here.

drops_with_progress.description:
Of the drops, the nodes with recorded progress (started, done, decided):
the answer does not undo it.

opens_decisions.description: Of those, the decisions that open: relevant and still to be answered.

Clause.description: A condition clause. The parser also holds the whole tree to 8 levels and 16 clauses, which JSON Schema cannot express.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

ClauseResolved.description: A condition clause. The parser also holds the whole tree to 8 levels and 16 clauses, which JSON Schema cannot express.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

decision.description: The decision whose answer is compared.

value.description: The value it is compared with.

decision.description: The decision whose answer is compared.

value.description: The value it is compared with.

Condition.description:
A `relevant_when` condition: a clause tree within `condition_depth_max` and
`condition_clause_count_max`, where clauses are the leaf predicates.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

ConditionResolved.description:
A `relevant_when` condition: a clause tree within `condition_depth_max` and
`condition_clause_count_max`, where clauses are the leaf predicates.

oneOf.description: The answer does not equal the value.
The answer is one of the values.
The answer (a list, or text) contains the value.

ConditionText.description: A compared value: a choice id, date, identity key, or text; at most body_bytes_max bytes.

anyOf.description: Every other answer type, as text.

ConditionValue.description:
The value a clause compares an answer with: a boolean, or text that the decision's
answer type gives meaning (a choice id, a date, an identity key, or plain text).

Conflict.description:
What a conflict is about, with the journey's side and the route's. A side that
is absent is `None` (an absent edge is `false`).

oneOf.description: A node field the journey edited and the route changed to something else.

dangling.description:
The route's value names a node the journey does not hold, so it cannot be taken
(a removed node's tombstone covers its subtree); only the journey's side is
offered.

oneOf.description: An explicit edge the journey added or removed, and the route the other way.
A participation the journey edited and the route changed to something else.
A resource the journey edited and the route changed to something else.

dangling.description:
The route's value names a node the journey does not hold, so it cannot be taken
(a removed node's tombstone covers its subtree); only the journey's side is
offered.

oneOf.description:
A node whose kind or answer type differs while the journey edited its shape or holds
state the change would invalidate: the whole node is in conflict.

answered.description: The journey has answered it, so taking an answer-type change reopens it.

dangling.description:
The route's value names a node the journey does not hold, so it cannot be taken
(a removed node's tombstone covers its subtree); only the journey's side is
offered.

oneOf.description: A decided decision whose answer names choices the route's choices no longer have.

rationale.description:
The rationale the journey's answer was given with, kept when the answer is
mapped onto the route's choices.

oneOf.description:
A role both sides changed, one whose new cardinality cannot hold the journey's direct
fill, or one the route removed that the journey still refers to.

insertions.description:
The insertions that map a segment role onto it, when the route removed it:
the role can then be kept or removed, not remapped.

members.description:
Who fills the role now, when insertions map onto it: removing it hands
these to the segment's nodes directly.

references.description: What in the journey refers to it.

route.description: The route's role, none when it removed it.

oneOf.description:
A participation kind both sides changed, or one the route removed that the journey
still uses.

insertions.description:
The insertions that map a segment kind onto it, when the route removed it:
the kind can then be kept or removed, not remapped.

references.description: The journey's participations of the kind, by node.

route.description: The route's kind, none when it removed it.

oneOf.description: The graph's `default_owner`, which both sides changed.

ConflictResolution.description:
How a reviewer resolves a conflict. Which resolutions a conflict offers depends
on what it is about ([`Conflict::offers`]); each becomes ordinary mutations when the
proposal is resolved.

oneOf.description: Keep the journey's value as a local edit, or its definition as an override.

Take the route's choices and map each removed choice the answer names to one that
remains (map old to new).
Take the route's value and clear the state it makes invalid.
Take the route's value and reopen the node.

Point every reference to a role the route removed at another role, then remove it.
Not offered while an insertion maps a segment role onto it.

role.description: The role the references move to.

oneOf.description:
Move every participation of a kind the route removed to another kind, then remove it.
Not offered while an insertion maps a segment kind onto it.

kind.description: The kind the participations move to.

oneOf.description:
Clear every reference to a role or kind the route removed, then remove it. Where an
insertion maps a segment role onto a removed role, the segment's nodes keep what the
role held: whoever filled it now fills their participations directly, and the
insertion's mapping goes with the role.

ConflictReview.description: What the engine offers for one conflict item.

item.description: The item's position in the proposal.

offers.description: The kinds of resolution the conflict offers, in the order a reviewer reads them.

removed_choices.description: For an answer conflict, the choices the answer names that the route no longer offers.

Consequences.description:
What an accepted patch or a proposal preview newly caused in derived state,
reported with the result and never stored.

into_scope.description:
Informational: nodes that were not relevant and are now relevant or undecided, in key
order.

out_of_scope.description: Informational: nodes that were in scope and are now not relevant, in key order.

stale.description: Nodes that became stale or gained a stale reason.

undecided.description: Finished nodes newly undecided, which may not apply: a warning, never a rejection.

unlocked.description:
Informational, never a warning: nodes newly on the acting frontier, in key order. A
node the write adds is not unlocked by it.

Constraint.description:
One constraint: `after` is at least `offset_days` after `before` (offsets may be zero or
negative).

conditional.description: It passes through an undecided node, so it may not apply.

days.description: The least number of days between them.

ConstraintSource.description: Where a constraint comes from, the kind then the nodes it names, colon-separated: `due_by:n_a`, `not_before:n_a`, `estimate:n_a`, `stage_close:n_stage`, `containment:n_parent:n_child`, or `dependency:n_a:n_b:` then `explicit`, `containment`, `inherited:n_ancestor`, `condition:n_decision` or `opening:n_stage`.

Contribution.description: A gravity or unlocks contribution: the node and how much it adds.

other_owner.description: It is owned by someone other than the node's owner (the owner factor of unlocks).

Conversation.description:
`GET /api/journeys/{id}/assistant` and `GET /api/routes/{id}/draft/assistant`: the caller's
conversation about that journey or draft (one per target per user), as kept: its
newest messages, oldest first. A conversation not started yet has none.

conversation.description: The conversation's id, which every turn about this target answers too.

oneOf.description: Cairn, reporting a write the assistant made or how a turn ended.

ConversationEntry.description: One kept message of a conversation.

ConversationId.description: Starts with "cv_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

Cursor.description:
A position in a projection's order: where the next page starts. Valid for the
same journey revision and derive inputs; a page read at another revision starts over.

Dangling.description:
One reference that would dangle, outside what a removal takes, with the mutation that
rewrites or removes it. It is sent in the same patch, before the removal.

mutation.description: The mutation that rewrites or removes it.

node.description: The node holding the reference; none for the graph's default owner.

DanglingKind.description: What a removal leaves dangling, by where the reference sits.

oneOf.description: A relevance condition reads what is removed.
A due-by rule measures from it.
A not-before rule measures from it.
A decision fills the removed role.
A participation names the removed role, or is of the removed kind.
The graph's default owner is the removed role.

DateLink.description: One authored date relationship between two nodes.

oneOf.description: A due-by or not-before rule on the node, measured from the source.

answer.description: The source is a date decision's answer, not a milestone.

days.description: The days between them, at least.

direction.description: Whether the node falls before or after the source.

oneOf.description: The stage must finish by its closing milestone.
The stage opens at the milestone for its dates only; nothing waits for it.
The decision's answer sets the milestone's date.

node.description: The node whose rule, bound or answer it is: the rule's node, the stage, the decision.

source.description:
The node it reads: the rule's milestone or date decision, the stage's milestone, the
milestone the decision sets.

DateOrigin.description:
Where a milestone's effective date comes from (pin, actual, and derived dates are
told apart).

oneOf.description: Its pin, set directly or by answering its feeding decision.

DateRule.description:
A date rule: `{before|after: <source(s)>, offset: <days>}`. Several sources are
several constraints; the offset defaults to 0.

DateRule2.description:
A date rule: `{before|after: <source(s)>, offset: <days>}`. Several sources are
several constraints; the offset defaults to 0.

DateRuleKind.description: Which date rule a date relationship is.

oneOf.description: The node is due before or after its source.
The node may not start before or after its source.

DecisionEntry.description: One decision in the decision view: its answer and which nodes the answer affects.

affects.description: The nodes whose relevance a condition reading it decides, their descendants included.

answer.description: Its answer, while in effect (decided and in scope).

display_state.description: The state every surface shows for it.

hidden_prerequisites.description: Its unsatisfied prerequisites that no drawn edge stands for (the marker on the card).

rationale.description: The rationale its answer was given with, while the answer is in effect.

DecisionView.description:
The graph filtered to decisions and their gating edges, with answers and what each
answer affected. A projection of the level with only decisions shown, not a separate
structure.

DeletedId.description:
A journey or route a hard delete removed: its id is never reused, so a late create cannot
bring it back.

oneOf.description: A route or segment, with its draft and every version.
A parent waiting on its child (Containment).

condition_on.description: The node whose condition creates the gate.

aliases.description:
Merged identities' old keys, each resolving to the identity it was merged into, at
most `alias_count_per_identity_max` resolving to one identity.

revision.description: The deployment revision.

DeriveInputs.description:
The inputs derive takes besides the journey,
supplied by the host and never read by the engine.

deployment.description: The deployment context: identities, emails, and aliases at a revision.

today.description: Today, in the deployment's time zone.

viewer.description: The viewer's identities, resolved from verified emails; usually one.

frontier.description: The frontier, ranked (Priority: ties by slack, gravity, key).

today.description: The today it was derived for.

DestinationAfter.description:
What a destination is once a proposal applies, as the engine works it out from the
candidate records: what the views draw in place of the destination.

oneOf.description: A journey as it would be, with the derive inputs its views are derived with.

A route as it would be: its header, its versions, its draft; and the latest version
when the candidate holds its graph (one the proposal publishes).

latest.description: The latest version after, when the candidate holds it.

oneOf.description: The deployment as it would be.

The destination does not exist after the candidate: a proposal to create it that
drafts nothing creating it yet, with nothing to draw.

DestinationNow.description: A proposal's destination as it is now.

name.description: Its name, when it exists and has one.

revision.description: Its revision; 0 when it does not exist.

Direction.description: Which way a date rule points.

oneOf.description: The node's instant falls at least `offset` days before each source.
The node's instant falls at least `offset` days after each source.

DisplayState.description:
The one state every surface shows for a node, composed from relevance, stored state,
effective skip, auto-done, blocking and snooze, and from the derived flags, which it leaves in
place. Stored state is what transitions act on; this is what people and agents read. The
first matching value in this order wins: `not_relevant`, `skipped`, `done`, `snoozed`,
`active`, `conditional`, `blocked`, `scheduled`, `ready`.

oneOf.description:
Nothing is in the way and nothing has started: actionable work, a container waiting
only on its own children with nothing started, or one ready to finish.

Started: stored `active`, or a container whose children are the only thing it waits
on and work beneath it has started (a deliverable or action under it is active or done).

In scope and unfinished, and its own or an inherited gate is unsatisfied. A container
is never blocked by its own children.

It may apply: relevance is `undecided` and it is unfinished, or relevance is
`not_relevant` but pending on an undecided decision (`pending_on`).

Unblocked and held for a date ahead: an `auto_done` milestone whose effective date is
ahead, another milestone whose pinned date is ahead, or unstarted work or a decision
whose own not-before date is ahead.
`done`, `decided`, a milestone done by its date, or a group that satisfies dependencies.
Does not apply, and settled (Gating): the recorded state survives beneath it.
The deployment: its identities and aliases.

DomainDocument.description:
The domain document: a journey's graph and state, the inputs to
derive it. Nothing derived is in it; proposals are not part of it.

DraftSource.description: Where a route draft comes from.

oneOf.description: Editing the latest published version (or an empty route).
Importing a route file; the import's content follows as ordinary mutations.
Saving a journey as a route; its structure follows as ordinary mutations.

Edge.description:
An explicit `requires` edge, identified by its two ends: `node` requires `requires`.
The graph document holds edges on the dependent node's `requires` list; changes and
removals name them this way.

EdgeEnd.description: One end of an edge an insertion adds: a node of the segment, or of the graph.

oneOf.description: A node by its key in the segment version.
A node by its key in the graph.

EdgeOrigin.description: How an edge on the canvas arose (implicit gates are drawn dotted).

oneOf.description: A condition gate: the dependent's condition reads the decision (Gating).

EffectiveDate.description:
A milestone's effective date: its actual date if done, else its pin, else its
derived due. What other constraints see when they reference it.

EffectiveParticipation.description: A node's effective participation of one kind.

Email.description: An email address, at most email_bytes_max (254) bytes; stored trimmed and lower-cased.

Ended.description: How a turn ended. The writes before any ending stand and are reported.

oneOf.description: The provider did not answer in time.
The provider answered with an error.
The provider refused the deployment's credential: the assistant is not set up.
The reply hit the output limit and is cut off; none of its tool calls ran.

The provider paused the reply, which the assistant does not continue; none of its
tool calls ran.
The model kept repeating a tool call that failed.
The model was still calling tools past the tool-loop limit.
The turn ran past the turn's time limit.

Event.description:
An append-only audit record of one mutation. The delta is the after-state of every
record the mutation wrote or removed, in order, so replay applies it with nothing
re-derived; events never hold derived values.

confirming_user.description: Who confirmed it, when a proposal was applied.

log.description:
The log it belongs to: its patch's domain, except a journey's deletion, which the
deployment log keeps.

ordinal.description: Its position in the patch, from 0.

patch_id.description: The patch it came from; a patch's events share it.

EventPage.description: A page of events; `next` is where the next page starts, absent on the last.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

EventType.description:
An event's type. Most mutations have one type; a few take theirs from
their content ([`Mutation::event_type`]).

ExplainedBlocker.description:
A list of explanation entries with its total: complete inside
the engine and the browser; a server response keeps the largest entries up to
`explanation_entry_count_max` and the total.

total.description: How many there are in all.

ExplainedContribution.description:
A list of explanation entries with its total: complete inside
the engine and the browser; a server response keeps the largest entries up to
`explanation_entry_count_max` and the total.

total.description: How many there are in all.

ExplainedField.description: A derived value whose explanation list a server response pages.

oneOf.description: The nodes that make up its gravity.
The nodes completing it would unblock.
The direct dependents completing it would not yet free, with what else each waits on.
The constraints and fixed dates of the chain behind its earliest start, in chain order.
The same for its latest start.
The same for its due date.
The same for the chain behind its shortfall.

ExplanationPage.description:
A page of one value's explanation list, `explanation_entry_count_max` at a time (largest
first; a date chain in chain order); the first page is what node detail carries.

constraints.description: The constraints of a date chain, in chain order; empty for the other fields.

entries.description: The entries of a gravity or unlocks list.

fixed.description: The dates fixed on a date chain; empty for the other fields.

held.description:
The entries of a still-waiting list, which holds dependents rather than
contributions; empty for the other fields.

next.description: Where the next page starts, when there is one.

total.description:
How many entries there are in all (for a date chain, constraints and fixed dates
together).

FixedBy.description: What fixes an instant on a chain: a pin, an actual date, a date answer, or today. A chain always ends at one of these.

oneOf.description: A pin, which a resolution may move.

An actual date, a fact that is never moved: a recorded start or finish, or the
journey's `created_at`.
A date decision's answer, which a revised answer moves.
Today, which holds unfinished work back: it starts, or finishes, no earlier.

FixedDate.description: A date fixed on a chain.

FrontierEntry.description:
One entry of the snapshot's acting frontier: enough to say what is next; the node's row is
in `list_nodes`.

ancestors.description: Its ancestors, root first: the breadcrumb.

display_state.description: The state every surface shows for the node.

rank.description: Its rank to three significant figures.

Graph.description:
The graph document (resolved): nodes, roles, and kinds by key, every reference a key,
and, for a journey, its state. Collections serialize
sorted by key, so a graph has one serialization.

default_owner.description: The role that owns nodes no ancestor gives an owner.

insertions.description: The segment insertions the graph holds.

retired_keys.description: Every key the graph has retired.

state.description: Journey state; empty for a route version or draft.

GraphId.description: Which graph a stored record belongs to.

GraphKey.description: The address of a record inside a graph, or of a whole node with everything on it.

oneOf.description: A node and everything attached to it.
A node's participation of one kind.
A note or link, with the node it is on when the address knows it.

GraphRecord.description: A record inside one graph: its content or, for a journey, its state.

oneOf.description: A node's participation of one kind.
An answer, with the rationale it was given with.

rationale.description: Why it was given; none when the answer gave no reason.

oneOf.description: A tombstone: a removed route-copied node.

Guard.description:
A transition guard: evidence a deliverable's or action's completion needs. Order is never
a guard.

oneOf.description: A `requires_artifact` deliverable has an artifact link.
A `requires_note` deliverable or action has a note of its own.
A `requires_checklist` deliverable or action has every checklist item ticked.
A placeholder has children or is atomic.

GuardFailure.description:
One specific guard failure: what a bypass records, so a later distinct failure
still produces `stale`.

oneOf.description: No artifact link on a `requires_artifact` deliverable.
No note on a `requires_note` deliverable or action.
A checklist item not ticked, on a `requires_checklist` deliverable or action.
A placeholder with no children that is not atomic.

Health.description:
`GET /healthz`: whether the server is serving. Answered 200 when it is, and 503 when its
store has failed closed and answers nothing until the process is restarted.

oneOf.description: The store has failed closed: every call errs until the process is restarted.

HeldDependent.description:
A dependent that completing a node would not yet free, and what else it waits on (
Priority: Unlocks): one entry of node detail's `still_waiting`.

also_waits_on.description:
What else it waits on, besides the node: its unsatisfied requirements, condition
gates, and stage openings, each with how it arose. Never empty.

node.description: The direct dependent that stays held.

HiddenByFilter.description:
The nodes the Filter's flag and owner settings hide, counted over the nodes of a kind
shown, within the level, under no collapse, not selected, and not settled as not relevant
(a ruled-out node is noise, and never counted here), among those the search keeps. A
node is counted once in `total` however many settings leave it out.

flags.description:
Per flag set (only mine included), the nodes that flag alone leaves out; a flag that
leaves none out has no entry.

owner.description: The nodes the owner setting alone leaves out.

total.description: The nodes any flag or the owner setting leaves out.

History.description: A page of a journey's history, or of one node's, grouped by patch.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

patches.description: At most a page of events, grouped by patch, in log order; a large patch spans pages.

Identity.description: A person or team journeys refer to, deployment-scoped.

emails.description:
Its emails, each held by at most one identity, at most
`email_count_per_identity_max`. A merge joins two identities' emails, so the engine checks
the joined set too.

name.description:
Its name, if it has one. An identity has a name, an email, or both, so one a
sign-in created from an account that gave no name is shown by its first email until
its person is asked for one.

IdentityKey.description: Starts with "who_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

IdentityReferences.description:
Everything that refers to an identity, directly or through an alias: every journey,
whatever its status, and every route whose draft or published versions do. Authoritative:
an identity with neither can be deleted.

InsertedEdge.description:
An edge an insertion adds: `node` requires `requires`, one end in the segment and the
other in the graph.

Insertion.description:
One placement of a segment version in a graph. Its local
edits are not stored: they are its members' differences from the version it is on.

key.description: The key, minted by the client like any new key; unique in the graph.

kinds.description: Each segment participation kind beyond `owner`, likewise.

nodes.description:
Its members: each graph node it copied that the graph still holds, with that node's
key in the segment.

parent.description: Where it was inserted: the parent the root went under, or none for the top level.

roles.description: Each segment role, mapped to the graph role it became.

segment.description: The segment and the version the insertion is on.

InsertionKey.description: Starts with "i_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

InsertionUse.description: One insertion of a segment version.

upgrade_available.description: Whether the segment has a later published version.

Instant.description: A point in time: `n_x.start` or `n_x.finish` for a node's start or finish, `n_x.answer` for a date decision's answered date, `created` for the journey's creation.

Journey.description: A journey domain: its fields, revision, and graph with state.

revision.description: The journey revision.

JourneyHeader.description: A journey's own fields, apart from its graph.

created_on.description:
The deployment-local calendar day it was created, the `created_at` date rules
measure from. Stored beside the timestamp so the engine never converts time
zones.

lineage.description: The route version it follows, if any.

owners.description: Who is responsible for the journey as a whole: zero or more identities.

JourneyId.description: Starts with "j_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

hits.description: Where the text was found, in order.

JourneyPage.description: A page of the journey index; `next` is where the next page starts, absent on the last.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page.

JourneyState.description:
A journey's state, on its graph document. Maps are keyed and sorted, so a state has one
serialization.

annotations.description:
Notes and links: on each node, and on the journey itself, at most
`note_count_per_node_max` notes and `link_count_per_node_max` links.

local_edits.description:
Each route-copied node's local edits, apart from its state so that an edit and
a transition on one node touch different records.

pins.description:
Pins: explicit journey-level dates on nodes. A pin from a
`feeds_milestone` answer is derived from the answer, not stored here.

rationales.description:
The rationale each answer was given with, by decision. A key here has an answer
beside it; an answer given without a reason has no entry, and reopening removes both.

role_fills.description:
Direct role fills, for roles without a filling decision. A role with a filling
decision is filled from that decision's answer, which is derived, not stored here.

ticks.description:
Each node's ticked checklist items. Each tick is its own record, kept apart from the
node's state so that ticking two items, or ticking and a transition, touch different
records. A node with no ticks has no entry.

tombstones.description: Route-copied nodes the journey removed, so an upgrade does not re-add them.

oneOf.description: Marked complete; still patchable, out of "mine" and cross-journey lists.
Archived: accepts only a move to active or completed, or hard deletion.

latest_version.description: The latest version its route has published.

owners.description:
Who owns it, each as the identity it names now (an alias read as the identity it was
merged into), once, in key order.

revision.description: Its revision.

upgrade_available.description: Whether its route has published a version newer than its own.

Kept.description:
A journey's deviation from its route that an upgrade keeps, listed for the reviewer (
locally edited and unchanged in the route).

oneOf.description: A marked edit on a route-copied node.
A participation kind the journey changed.
The graph's `default_owner`, which the journey changed.

KindChoice.description: What a segment participation kind becomes in the graph it is inserted into.

oneOf.description: A new kind, minted from the insertion.

KindKey.description: Starts with "k_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

LabeledChoice.description:
A choice with a label, as written. Unknown fields are an error, so a misspelled or
unsupported attribute is never silently dropped.

Level.description:
One aggregation level of the canvas: the visible nodes for the shown kinds within the
drilled-in container, the edges re-targeted to visible stand-ins with duplicates collapsed,
and each container's roll-ups. Display only: stored state stays on each node.

collapsed.description: The containers collapsed that took effect: those within the level.

container.description: The drilled-in container; none for the whole journey.

date_links.description:
The date relationships between the selected card and the stand-ins of the other ends,
sorted by their ends; empty when nothing is selected. Not edges: nothing waits on them.

display.description: The relevance classes shown; every class when absent.

edges.description: The edges, sorted by their ends.

hidden_by_class.description:
The count, per relevance class left out: the nodes hidden only for their class (of a
kind shown, within the level, under no collapse, not left out by `top`, and kept by the
filters), so showing a class draws exactly that many more. Empty when every class is
shown.

hidden_by_filter.description:
What the level's flag and owner filters leave out, among the nodes the search keeps and
that would otherwise be drawn. Empty when no flag or owner filter is set.

nodes.description: The visible nodes, in tree order.

LevelDateLink.description: The date relationships drawn at a level between the stand-ins of their ends.

from.description:
The stand-in of the earlier end where some relationship fixes the order, else of the
source.

links.description: The relationships it stands for, sorted; never empty.

orders.description:
Some relationship it stands for fixes the order: the end `to` can never come before
the end `from`.

to.description:
The stand-in of the later end where some relationship fixes the order, else of the
node whose dates they are.

LevelDisplay.description:
Which nodes a level shows by how their relevance reads to a person. A node is
`relevant` when it applies; `conditional` when it may apply (its relevance is undecided,
or it is not relevant only because the decision it reads cannot be answered yet); and
`not_relevant` when it is settled as not applying (ruled out by an answer, a skip, or a
closed branch).

oneOf.description: May apply: undecided, or waiting on a decision that cannot be answered yet.

LevelEdge.description:
An edge drawn at a level, between the nearest visible stand-ins of its ends, with the
edges it collapses.

from.description: The stand-in of the requirement side.

implicit.description: Every underlying edge is implicit (drawn dotted).

to.description: The stand-in of the dependent side.

underlying.description: The edges it stands for, sorted; never empty.

LevelNode.description: One visible node at a level.

display_state.description: The state every surface shows for the node.

hidden_prerequisites.description:
Its hidden, unsatisfied prerequisites that no visible edge stands for: the "hidden
prerequisites" marker, which opens the trace. Empty when it has none.

kept_work_pending.description: A skipped container, or a group marked done, whose kept work is not yet done.

parent.description:
Its nearest visible ancestor within the level, which it is drawn under; none at the
top level.

rolled_up.description:
The hidden nodes that roll up into it (a hidden action is a checklist item on its
deliverable), in tree order.

Lineage.description: A journey's link to the route version it was created from or last upgraded to.

LinkedLogin.description: One login a user signs in with.

name.description: The name the provider gave the account at the last sign-in, if it gave one.

provider.description: The provider, by its configured name.

subject.description: The provider's subject for the account.

verified_emails.description:
The emails the provider marked verified at the last sign-in; only these match an
identity.

ListFlag.description: A list filter that needs no argument.

oneOf.description: A decision that can be answered now.
Placeholders that still need to be broken down.

Showing the display state `blocked`: a gate it waits on is unsatisfied (a container's
own children never count).
Finished, but a completing guard would now fail.
Its plan can no longer be met.

next.description: Where the next page starts, when there is one.

total.description: How many rows the query matches in all.

LocalEdit.description:
What a journey changed on a route-copied node, so an upgrade leaves it alone. A
marker carries no reason.

oneOf.description: The node's explicit edge to the named requirement (added or removed).
The node's participation of a kind.

The node's kind or, for a decision, its answer type: what a replacement changes that
no single field edit can.

Location.description: Where a violation is: listed by path, specific enough to fix without reading source.

mutation.description: The mutation's position in the patch, when one mutation caused it.

path.description: The node's path in the graph the patch would produce.

LoggedEvent.description: An event and its position in the log, which orders history and pages it.

seq.description: The position: increasing in commit order.

Markdown.description: Markdown, at most body_bytes_max (64 KiB) bytes.

McpAccess.description: How an agent reaches this host's MCP server.

sign_in.description: How an agent signs in, in the order the providers are asked; empty when it cannot.

tokens.description: Whether a person can make agent tokens here, and list and revoke theirs.

url.description: The MCP endpoint's absolute address: the public URL joined with the MCP path.

decision.description: The decision whose answer is tested.
The decision whose answer is tested.

Mine.description: The nodes the caller participates in.

entries.description: The nodes, in key order, each with the participation kinds the caller holds on it.

MineEntry.description: A node the viewer participates in, with the kinds they hold.

acting.description: On the acting frontier: nothing holds it back now.

kinds.description: The participation kinds the viewer holds on it.

open.description: Still the viewer's to do: an item (not a group) in scope and not finished or skipped.

MintedToken.description: A token just minted: the one time its secret is seen.

agent.description: The agent the token acts as.

token.description: The bearer token; Cairn keeps only its digest.

Mutation.description:
One change within a patch, each emitting one event. The
set covers every change a patch can make; [`Mutation::change_class`] sorts each into
structural or state.

oneOf.description: Create the target journey, empty or from a route version.

from.description: The route version to copy, or none for an empty journey.

owners.description:
Who is responsible for the journey as a whole; none when absent. Nobody is an
owner by default, the creator included.

oneOf.description:
Rename or redescribe the journey, or change its owners. The description is set as
given (absent clears it).

owners.description:
Who is responsible for the journey as a whole: absent keeps the owners it has, a
list replaces them, an empty list clears them.

oneOf.description: Create the target route, with no versions and no draft.

kind.description: Process (the default) or segment; fixed from here on.

oneOf.description: Retire the route (hide it from new-journey creation) or bring it back.
Publish the draft as the next version and clear it.
Change one field of a node.

value.description: The field and its new value.

oneOf.description: Replace a node whole, as a kind or answer-type change does.
Remove a node and everything its removal names.
Change a role's id, title, or cardinality.

role.description: The role as it should be.

oneOf.description: Remove a role no participation or `fills_role` references.
Change a participation kind's id, title, or cardinality.

kind.description: The kind as it should be.

oneOf.description: Remove a participation kind nothing references.
Set or clear the graph's `default_owner` role.
Set a node's participation of one kind.
Remove a node's participation of one kind, restoring inheritance.
Add a resource to a node.

resource.description: The resource as it should be.

oneOf.description:
Insert a published segment version under a parent, wired to the graph's own nodes and
with its roles and kinds mapped, in one event.

edges.description: The wiring: each edge joins one segment node and one node of the graph.

insertion.description: The insertion's key, new in the graph.

kinds.description: What each segment participation kind becomes, likewise.

omit.description: Segment nodes left out, each with its subtree.

parent.description: The group, deliverable, or action the root goes under; none for the top level.

roles.description:
What each segment role becomes; a role not named takes the graph's role with its
id and cardinality, else is added.

root_id.description: The root's id; the segment root's own, suffixed when a sibling has it, if none.

root_title.description: The root's title; the segment root's own if none.

segment.description: The segment and one of its published versions.

oneOf.description:
Move a node, whatever it waits on: start, stop, complete (work and milestones),
skip, reopen, or `mark_done` (a group only).

Answer or revise a decision. The rationale belongs to this answer alone: a
revision that gives none leaves the decision without one.

rationale.description: Why it was given: markdown, free text under the body limit.

oneOf.description: Edit a recorded start or finish date.
Fill a role without a filling decision.
Move a pin by a number of days (`shift`).

Snooze an actionable node, or a container (a group, or work with children) that has
work left beneath it, which holds every descendant off the acting frontier.

until.description: Until a date or a node.

oneOf.description:
Lift a snooze. A node held only through a container's snooze is refused, naming
the container to unsnooze instead.
Mark a placeholder atomic, or not.

Tick or untick one checklist item. Setting an item to the state it has changes
nothing.

Move the journey to a newer version of its route, taking every clean outcome of the
three-way merge (route changes it did not edit, new nodes, orphans); conflict
resolutions and orphan removals ride after it in the same patch as ordinary mutations.

Link the journey to the version its saved route published, in one event: the
lineage, each node the version holds route-copied and marked exactly where it differs,
every other node local, and the version's roles and kinds the journey lacks.
Change a node's provenance, as an upgrade orphaning it does.
Set or clear a local-edit marker (reset to route clears it).
Create an identity; may ride in any patch.
Change an identity's name or emails (deployment).

identity.description: The identity as it should be.

oneOf.description:
Merge identities into one that remains (deployment): every merged identity's emails
move to the survivor and each merged key becomes an alias of it, all checked against one
snapshot.

journeys.description:
Every journey referencing the survivor or any merged identity, at the revision the
merge was checked against; at most `journey_count_per_merge_max`.

merged.description:
The identities merged into it, whose keys become aliases; at least one, at most
`identity_count_per_fill_max`.

oneOf.description:
Delete an identity nothing refers to (deployment): the identity, its emails, and
every alias resolving to it. Rejected while any journey, route draft, or route version
refers to it or to one of its aliases; the commit rechecks that none does.

Delete a journey and its events for good (deployment): the deployment log keeps who
deleted it and when, and its id is never used again. Rejected when the journey is not
at `revision`; the commit rechecks it.

revision.description: The journey's revision, as read.

oneOf.description:
Delete a route or segment with its draft, every version, and its events, for good
(deployment): only while no journey's lineage and no insertion names any of its
versions. Its id is never used again. Rejected when the route is not at `revision`; the
commit rechecks the revision and that nothing has started using it.

revision.description: The route's revision, as read.

oneOf.description: Apply a proposal to its destination: its mutations follow its own revision check.

reviewed_revision.description: The proposal revision the user reviewed.

Mutations.description:
A journey's or route's mutations in one patch: at least one, at most
`mutation_count_per_patch_max`, in the order they apply.

Next.description:
The acting frontier ordered, each item with its breadcrumb and why it ranks where it
does; when it is empty, what the journey waits on.

stalled.description: The stalled diagnostic, when the journey is stalled.

NodeDates.description: A node's derived dates. Every bound is null when nothing reaches it.

effective_date.description: A milestone's effective date; none for other kinds, or when nothing gives one.

links.description:
The date relationships it has directly, in both directions: its own rules, bounds and
answer, and the ones that read it. Sorted.

not_before.description:
The earliest its own not-before rules let it start: the latest of each source's
earliest date plus the rule's offset. Work or a decision whose date this is, while it
is after today, is scheduled: off the acting frontier, though it can still be started
or finished. None when it has no such rule, or no source has a date.

overdue_days.description:
How many days its due is before today, for an overdue node; none when it is
not overdue.

shortfall.description: The plan can no longer be met.

slack_days.description: Latest start minus today; null is "no deadline".

NodeDerived.description:
Every derived value for one node, with the inputs that explain it. The flags are its own,
each independent of the others, so they stay booleans rather than a state enum.

answer.description:
A decision's answer while it is in effect (decided and relevant), identities read
through aliases; none for any other node, and for a decision out of scope or undecided.

blocked_by.description:
What blocks it itself: its own explicit requirements, condition gates, and stage
opening, and its children, each unsatisfied. What it inherits is listed once, on the
ancestor that holds it (`blocked_through`), never copied onto each descendant. A node
that is not blocked lists what its own requirements, conditions, and opening still
hold back beneath it.

blocked_through.description:
The ancestors, nearest first, whose own unsatisfied requirements, openings, or
conditions block it through containment; each lists them in its own `blocked_by`.

checklist_count.description: How many checklist items are ticked; none for a node with no items.

display_state.description:
The state every surface shows for the node, composed from relevance, stored state
and the flags beside it, which stay as they are.

done_by_date.description: A pending auto-done milestone that reads as done.

failing_guards.description:
The bypassable guards completing it (a deliverable or action) would fail if attempted
now with no bypass in the patch: the evidence it still lacks. Empty for every other
node, and for one finished or not relevant.

kept_work_pending.description:
For a skipped container or a group marked done: the kept work beneath it that is not
yet done, which its dependents still wait for. Empty otherwise.

membership_lost.description: Its seeding identity left the role it was broken down by.

moves.description:
The moves the node accepts now: the transitions its kind's table has from its stored
state, those that need the node in scope only while it is, a completion only while its
guards hold (else `complete_anyway`), and `insert_segment` where it may hold children.

needs_breakdown.description: A placeholder with no children that is not atomic.

open.description:
Still to do and in scope: relevant or undecided, and not finished or skipped. A group
is open until its own finish is satisfied.

overdue.description: Non-terminal with its due before today.

progress.description:
A container's progress over the work beneath it; none for a node with no
children.

rank.description: Rank, for nodes in the normalization set.

skip_count.description:
How many items (nodes that are not groups) a skip of the node covers: the in-scope,
unfinished ones beneath it, leaving out work marked Keep with what is inside it, and
what a nearer container already skips. Once the node is skipped, or is a group marked
done, these are the items that read skipped through it; before, the items marking it
done would skip.

skipped_by.description:
The ancestor whose skip, or whose marking done, skips it; absent when it is not
skipped through an ancestor.

skips_beneath.description:
Whether the node skips the unfinished work beneath it, and so carries the reason it was
given: it is skipped, or a group marked done.

snoozable.description:
Whether a snooze can sit on the node: it is in scope with something left to do, and a
group has work in scope left beneath it.

snoozed.description:
A snooze that holds over the node: its own, else the one of the container it is
held through (`snoozed_via`).

snoozed_via.description:
The container whose snooze holds over the node, the reason a descendant names.
Set even when the node's own snooze holds as well, so a node snoozed twice names its
container and shows its own target in `snoozed`.

stale.description:
Why a finished node is stale: a dependency it relied on was reopened, or evidence its
completion needed is now missing.

subtree_gravity.description:
A container's subtree gravity (Priority): what rides on its whole area, the counted
weight of the container and its open descendants and everything downstream of any of
them, each once. Never less than any member's `gravity`; none for a node with no
children.

unassigned.description:
No owner, for a non-group node that is in scope and unfinished; a not-relevant or
finished node, or a group, never is.

unlocks_from.description: The nodes completing this would unblock.

waits_on.description:
The unsatisfied gate dependencies that hold the node now, its own and
those it inherits through its ancestors (requirements, conditions, openings), its
children aside; one entry per dependency, its nearest holder's; empty when nothing
holds it. `blocked_by` and `blocked_through` explain the structure; this answers
"what does it wait on".

NodeDetail.description:
One node in full. Its explanation lists (`derived.gravity_from`, `unlocks_from`)
carry their largest entries up to `explanation_entry_count_max` with their totals; the rest
page through the node's explanations endpoint.

annotations.description: The notes and links on it, in key order.

answer_effects.description:
A decision's effects per choice: what each answer brings in, drops, and leaves
to be decided later, with the role it fills and the milestone it pins.

children.description: Its children in key order, each with its state.

derived.description: Every derived value with what explains it.

local_edits.description: What the journey edited on it, for a route-copied node.

node.description: The node: description, resources, participations as written, and its kind's payload.

rationale.description: The rationale the recorded answer was given with, markdown.

record.description: Its stored state, provenance, and actual dates.

still_waiting.description:
The direct dependents completing it would not yet free, each with what else it waits
on (Priority: Unlocks): the largest entries with the total; page the rest with
the explanations endpoint, field `still_waiting`.

oneOf.description: The weight; in a journey, a weight override.

NodeFieldValueResolved.description: A new value for one node field.

oneOf.description: A new parent, or none to make the node a root.
A new weight, or none for the kind's default.
A new checklist; empty clears it.

NodeKey.description: Starts with "n_"; at most id_bytes_max (64) bytes.

NodeMove.description:
A move a node accepts now, as a patch of that one move would find it: the engine's answer to
what can be done to the node, for every surface to offer and none to work out again.

oneOf.description:
`complete_anyway`: completing would fail a guard, and this goes ahead past it. Absent
while `complete` is accepted.
Answering the decision, a first answer or a revision.
A segment inserted under the node: any node but a decision or milestone holds children.

NodeRef.description:
A node named in one of the snapshot's lists: its key and its title, so the list says what
each is without a second read.

NodeRow.description:
One node as a row of the list, the next list, or the snapshot: what it is,
where it sits, and its derived signals.

actionable.description: Whether work can be started on it now: relevant, not blocked, and not finished.

ancestors.description: Its ancestors, root first: the breadcrumb.

checklist_count.description: How many checklist items are ticked; none for a node with no items.

display_state.description: The state every surface shows for the node.

needs_breakdown.description: Whether it is a placeholder that still needs to be broken down into children.

overdue.description: Non-terminal with its due before today.

rank.description: Its rank and terms, for nodes in the normalization set.

shortfall_days.description: Days the plan can no longer be met by.

slack_days.description: Latest start minus today; none is no deadline.

snoozed.description: A snooze that holds over the node: its own, else its container's.

snoozed_via.description: The container whose snooze holds over the node.

stale.description: A terminal node whose completing guards would now fail.

state.description:
Its stored state: what transitions act on. Prefer `display_state` for "what is its
status".

unlocks.description: Unlocks: the viewer's, in a ranking for them.

NodeState.description: One node's stored state in a journey.

atomic.description: A placeholder marked atomic, so it can complete without children.

finished_on.description:
When the node finished: the actual date a milestone was done, the day a
decision was decided or work was done.

finished_revision.description:
The journey revision the finish was recorded at, which orders it against reopens of
what it relied on; held exactly when the finish's day is.

reason.description:
Why the node was skipped, or why a group was marked done, while it is (both require
a reason).

reopened.description:
Its latest reopen of a finish, while it has not finished again: what finished work
that relied on it reads to go stale. None after reopening a skip or a mark done, which
left nothing to rely on.

started_on.description: When a deliverable or action was started; editable like an actual date.

Notice.description: One advisory finding about a node of a route graph.

message.description: A sentence for people, generated for display.

path.description: The node's path, to open it by.

NoticeCode.description: What a notice is about. One exists today; each later advisory finding adds a code.

oneOf.description:
A node with no chain to or from the graph's `final` milestone, so neither its priority
nor its dates feel that milestone.

OpenDecision.description: An open decision and who owns it.

OutlineFact.description:
One thing a proposal does to its destination's own header or lifecycle, as a fact
the listing and the review word the same way.

oneOf.description: Moves the journey to a newer version of its route.
Links the journey to the version its saved route published.

OutsideReference.description:
One place outside a removed subtree that names a node inside it, and so must be
rewritten or removed in the same patch.

holder.description: The node outside that holds the reference.

target.description: The node inside the subtree it names.

oneOf.description: Exempt the node's subtree from an ancestor's skip.

bypass.description: A guard bypass on the node's transition.

force_include.description: Treat the node as relevant despite conditions (Gating, Force include).

keep.description: Exempt the node and its subtree from an ancestor's skip.

ParticipationKind.description: A participation kind a graph declares beyond the built-in `owner`.

id.description: The id, unique in the graph.

key.description: The stable key: optional in a file.

multi.description: Held by several identities rather than one.

ParticipationKindResolved.description: A participation kind a graph declares beyond the built-in `owner`.

id.description: The id, unique in the graph.

key.description: The stable key: optional in a file.

multi.description: Held by several identities rather than one.

ParticipationMapping.description: What becomes of an explicit identity's participations when a journey is saved as a route.

oneOf.description: Map it to an existing role.

all_blocked.description: Every in-scope non-terminal node is blocked: shown as "blocked".

is `not_relevant`. Prefer it to `by_state` for "how is the journey doing".

open_decisions.description: Open, in-scope decisions with their owners, in rank order.

remaining.description: In-scope nodes with work left on them.

shortfalls.description: Nodes with a shortfall, by key.

upcoming_milestones.description: In-scope milestones not yet done that have a date, earliest first.

total.description: How many there are in all.

entries.description: The dates, earliest first, then by key.

undated.description: In-scope milestones with no date yet.

final.description: The journey's `final` milestone: the end anchor.

origin.description: Where the date comes from: a milestone's actual, a pin, or a derived due date.

overdue.description: Non-terminal with its due before today.

shortfall_days.description: Days the plan can no longer be met by.

Trace.description:

downstream.description:

key order.

gravity_contributors.description: The nodes in `downstream` that contribute to its gravity, in key order.

upstream.description:

order.

start or finish records default to today and are edited with

records which. Only a deliverable or action has guards to bypass.

reason.description: Why, when the person gave a reason. Leave the field out for none.

oneOf.description: To `skipped`, with the reason a skip requires.

work inside it reads skipped, as under a skip, until it is reopened.

actions.description:

conversation.description: The conversation the turn was added to: the user's, about its target.

reply.description: What the assistant said last, if anything.

unanswered.description: The open decisions its relevance waits on that it newly waits on.

dependent.description: The node whose `requires`, condition, or opening it is.

item.description: The item's position in the proposal.

the route it follows.

proposal.description: The proposal's id, generated by the client.

name.description:

their login gave, else its first verified email.

VersionJourneys.description: One published version and the journeys on it.

insertions.description: Where this version of a segment is inserted.

journeys.description: The journeys whose lineage is this version.

completion and the mutation that gave it an unfinished dependency in the same patch).

id.

related.description: Other keys involved: a cycle's members, the other holder of a duplicate.
